counterevidence_considered.description: The report explicitly states, consistently with the code, that repeated inspections were not entered as separate observations and that inference used one value per housing; the reported sample sizes are n = 9 housings per group, not 36 rows per group.

source_refs.quoted_text:
The four inspections of a given housing are repeated measurements of the same
mooring and are not independent of one another, so they were not entered into the
group comparison as separate observations. Each housing was first summarised by
the ordinary least-squares slope of biofilm cover on month index, that is, its
fouling accumulation rate in percentage points per month. That reduction yields
exactly one analysed value per independently moored housing, and the 18 rates were
compared between coatings with Welch's two-sample t-test for unequal variances
(two-sided).

Epoxy control: mean rate 7.79 pp/month (SD 0.69, n = 9 housings).
Silicone-hydrogel topcoat: mean rate 3.84 pp/month (SD 0.48, n = 9 housings).

counterevidence_considered.description: Reported test statistics are numerically consistent with an 18-slope analysis rather than a 72-row analysis: with group SDs 0.69 and 0.48 at n = 9 each, SE = sqrt(0.69^2/9 + 0.48^2/9) ~ 0.28 and t = 3.95/0.28 ~ 14.1, matching the reported t = 14.00; the Welch df of 14.3 is bounded by 16 (9+9-2), whereas a row-level t-test would show df near 70.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: reported df = 14.3 (consistent with n = 9 + 9 slopes; inconsistent with 72 rows)

looks at the same mooring rather than four separate moorings. They describe how

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to show the issue was present by tracing every input to stats.ttest_ind in workflow/analysis.py: the arrays passed are built from the per-housing `rate` dict (one polyfit slope per housing_id), not from raw rows, so no housing contributes more than one observation to the row-independent procedure. I then checked whether the report's numbers could secretly reflect a 72-row analysis: a row-level Welch test would give degrees of freedom near 70, but the reported df = 14.3 is consistent only with 9-vs-9 per-housing samples, and recomputing t from the reported group means/SDs at n = 9 (SE ~ 0.28, t ~ 14.1) reproduces the reported t = 14.00. I also spot-checked slopes against data/input.csv (H01: covers 4.2, 12.0, 19.1, 27.3 over months 0-3 give an OLS slope of ~7.64, matching the report table). All checks confirm one entry per independent unit; the falsification attempt failed.
